newsitem.title: GERMANY: German producer prices tick up again in May.
newsitem.headline: German producer prices tick up again in May.

text.p: German producer prices posted their largest year-on-year increase in May since December 1995, rising by 1.1 percent after an increase of 0.9 percent in April, official data showed on Monday.
Producer prices were up by 0.2 percent in May compared to April, when they rose by 0.3 percent, the Federal Statistics Office said.

Upstream price pressures have increased somewhat since the sharp depreciation of the German mark against the dollar started last summer, but most economists say the inflation environment remains benign.
In western Germany, producer prices rose in May by 0.1 percent month-on-month and by 1.0 percent against the same month a year earlier.
In the formerly communist east, producer prices rose more sharply, by a monthly 0.6 percent and 2.4 percent year-on-year.

Detailing price changes, the statistics office said that non-ferrous metals and scrap metal rose by 3.4 percent in May from April, iron and steel rose by 1.0 percent, while prices for office and data processing equipment fell by 1.2 percent.

In western Germany, prices rose for electrolyte copper (+10.4 percent), fresh pork (+6.7), reinforced concrete slabs (+5.3), roast coffee (+4.1), scrap copper (+3.8), reinforcing steel (+3.7) and polyvinyl chloride (PVC) (+2.5).
Prices fell for liquefied gas by 7.1 percent, as well as for bitumen (-6.5 percent), asphalt (-6.4) and fertilisers (-4.4)
